subject: surgery
title: Small Bowel Tumours, Carcinoids, and Fistulas

steps.tx: Despite accounting for seventy-five percent of the length and ninety percent of the mucosal surface area of the digestive tract, primary **small bowel tumours** are remarkably rare, constituting less than five percent of all gastrointestinal neoplasms. Protective factors suppressing small bowel oncogenesis include rapid liquid transit limiting carcinogen exposure, high concentrations of detoxifying enzymes like benzpyrene hydroxylase, and abundant secretory immunoglobulin A.
steps.say: Small bowel tumours are rare despite the large surface area, protected by rapid transit, low bacterial counts, and high mucosal immunity.

vis.caption: Small bowel tumours. Illustration: StewardMD original.

steps.tx: Malignant small bowel neoplasms are categorized into four principal histological subtypes: neuroendocrine tumours, adenocarcinomas, gastrointestinal stromal tumours, and lymphomas. Duodenal adenocarcinomas arise predominantly around the ampulla of Vater. Primary gastrointestinal stromal tumours predominate in the jejunum and express CD117 (c-kit), whereas intestinal **lymphoma** occurs most frequently in the ileum due to the concentration of lymphoid follicles in Peyer patches.
steps.say: Small bowel malignancies include neuroendocrine tumours, adenocarcinomas, stromal tumours, and lymphomas, varying by anatomical location.

rows: Bulky mass, high perforation risk with chemo

steps.tx: The most common primary malignancy of the small intestine is the neuroendocrine **carcinoid tumour**, originating from subepithelial enterochromaffin cells of Kulchitsky. Predominating in the distal ileum, these slow-growing tumours secrete bioactive amines including serotonin, bradykinin, and prostaglandins. Over thirty percent are multicentric, and locally secreted serotonin induces an intense fibroblastic desmoplastic reaction in the adjacent mesentery, causing kinking, foreshortening, and bowel obstruction.
steps.say: Carcinoid tumours arise from enterochromaffin cells in the ileum, causing an intense mesenteric fibrotic reaction that kinks the intestine.

nodes.label: Enterochromaffin Cells of Kulchitsky in Crypts of Lieberkuhn
Local Hypersecretion of Serotonin & Vasoactive Peptides
Subacute Mechanical Small Bowel Obstruction & Ischemia

steps.tx: Ordinarily, serotonin released into portal circulation is rapidly metabolized and cleared during first-pass transit by hepatic monoamine oxidase into five-hydroxyindoleacetic acid. However, when an intestinal carcinoid metastasizes to the liver or drains directly into systemic veins, vasoactive mediators bypass hepatic degradation, precipitating classic **carcinoid syndrome**. The syndrome manifests with episodic cutaneous flushing of the face and neck, secretory watery diarrhoea, bronchospasm, and tricuspid endocardial fibrosis.
steps.say: Carcinoid syndrome occurs when liver metastases release serotonin into systemic circulation, causing flushing, diarrhoea, and right-sided valvular disease.

rows: Sudden paroxysmal erythema of face, neck, and upper chest
Stimulates intestinal motility and fluid secretion
Tricuspid regurgitation and pulmonary stenosis (right heart)

steps.tx: Biochemical confirmation of carcinoid syndrome is established by measuring twenty-four hour urinary excretion of five-hydroxyindoleacetic acid. Serum chromogranin A serves as a reliable circulating biomarker of neuroendocrine tumour burden. Diagnostic imaging employs Gallium-68 DOTATATE positron emission tomography, which binds somatostatin receptors with remarkable sensitivity. Medical management utilizes long-acting **octreotide** to block hormone release, while surgical resection of the primary and accessible hepatic metastases provides symptom relief.
steps.say: Diagnosis relies on 24-hour urine 5-HIAA and Gallium-68 DOTATATE scans, managed with somatostatin analogues like octreotide.

nodes.label: Ga-68 DOTATATE PET-CT Localizes Somatostatin Receptors
Symptom Control with Long-Acting Somatostatin Analogues
Cytoreductive Hepatic Resection & Primary En Bloc Excision

steps.tx: An abnormal, epithelialized communication connecting the lumen of the intestine directly to the external skin surface is defined as an **enterocutaneous fistula**. Greater than eighty percent of all enterocutaneous fistulas arise iatrogenically as postoperative surgical complications following inadvertent enterotomy during adhesiolysis, anastomotic breakdown, or erosion from synthetic mesh and rigid abdominal drains.
steps.say: An enterocutaneous fistula connects intestinal lumen to skin, usually arising as a postoperative complication after surgery.

steps.tx: Enterocutaneous fistulas are categorized by twenty-four hour fluid output into low-output under two hundred millilitres, moderate-output from two hundred to five hundred millilitres, and high-output fistulas exceeding five hundred millilitres daily. High-output fistulas originating from the duodenum or proximal jejunum trigger catastrophic fluid depletion, severe electrolyte disturbances, profound zinc deficiency, and corrosive skin breakdown, demanding intensive parenteral fluid and nutritional **resuscitation**.
steps.say: Fistulas are classified by daily output, with high-output fistulas discharging over 500 mL and provoking severe dehydration.

rows: Total parenteral nutrition mandatory; bowel rest
Enteral feeding if tract length allows
Standard enteral nutrition or oral diet

steps.tx: The conditions that prevent spontaneous closure of an enterocutaneous fistula are summarized by the surgical mnemonic **FRIENDS**. These factors encompass Foreign body, Radiation enteritis, Infection or epithelialization, Neoplasm, Distal obstruction, and Short fistula tract under two centimetres. Initial management adheres to the SNAP protocol prioritizing Sepsis control, Nutritional support, Anatomical delineation, and Planned definitive operative repair delayed for four to six months.
steps.say: Factors preventing fistula closure are remembered by the FRIENDS mnemonic, managed with the SNAP protocol deferring surgery for four to six months.
